name: ALPS II apparatus
notes: No placements[] entry recorded: a fetched source explicitly confirming ALPS II sits in the DESY 'HERA North Hall' (site:desy-hera-north-hall-h1, owned by the facilities lead) was not found this session; forcing that reference without confirmation would violate A17. See worklog.

summary.plain: ALPS II shines a laser at a wall to see if a tiny fraction of the light can sneak through as an undetectable particle and turn back into light on the far side, which would be a sign of new, very light particles.
summary.technical: Light-shining-through-a-wall (LSW) apparatus reusing decommissioned HERA superconducting dipole magnets and optical build-up/regeneration cavities at DESY, operating since 2023-05-23.

technology.note: No light-shining-through-walls value exists in the ontology's technology_classes enum; recorded as 'other' (see worklog).
technology.value: Light-shining-through-a-wall apparatus: a laser beam is enhanced in a build-up optical cavity, blocked by a light-tight wall, with a second, identical regeneration cavity and superconducting dipole magnets (reused HERA magnets) on both sides, and a low-noise single-photon/heterodyne detector looking for regenerated photons on the far side.
